bib.title: Understanding Back-Translation at Scale
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 2018 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (EMNLP), pages 489-500

question: How should synthetic source sentences be generated for back-translation in NMT, and how far does back-translation scale with hundreds of millions of monolingual sentences?
hypothesis: Beam and greedy (MAP) outputs are too regular and do not cover the true data distribution, so sampling or noised beam outputs should give a richer training signal.
contributions: Comprehensive comparison of methods to generate synthetic sources (greedy, beam, sampling, top-k sampling, beam+noise)
Analysis of why non-MAP synthetic data gives a stronger training signal (training loss, language-model perplexity)
Comparison of synthetic data to genuine bitext and of domain effects, in a controlled setup
Scaling to 226M monolingual sentences for a new state of the art on WMT'14 En-De (35 BLEU) and 45.6 BLEU on En-Fr

method.summary: Train a reverse (target-to-source) Big Transformer on WMT bitext, use it to translate target-language monolingual newscrawl into synthetic sources by greedy, beam, sampling, top10 or beam+noise, add the synthetic pairs to the bitext and train the forward Transformer. Compare generation methods, low-resource vs high-resource, domain, bitext upsampling, then scale up.
method.task: neural machine translation with monolingual data (back-translation data augmentation)

datasets.name: WMT'18 English-German bitext (no ParaCrawl)
datasets.split: dev newstest2012; test newstest2013-2017; plus 52K held-out pairs from the training data (valid-mixed)
datasets.preprocessing: removed sentences longer than 250 words and pairs with source/target length ratio above 1.5; Moses tokenizer; joint BPE with 35K types

datasets.name: WMT'14 English-French bitext
datasets.preprocessing: filtered as for En-De; joint BPE with 44K types

models.name: Big Transformer (forward and backward)
models.architecture: encoder-decoder Transformer, fairseq re-implementation in pytorch

training.objective: maximum likelihood of target given source, with label smoothing 0.1 (uniform prior)
training.steps: 30K updates bitext only; 50K with 3M synthetic; 75K with 6M and 12M; 100K with 24M; En-Fr 300K; En-De 226M run 250K
training.hardware: 16 DGX-1 machines x 8 Nvidia V100 GPUs (128 GPUs), Infiniband, NCCL2
training.wall_clock: bitext only 3h20min; 6M and 12M synthetic 7h30min; 24M synthetic 10h15min; En-Fr 27h40min (300K updates); En-De 226M 22.5 hours (250K updates), all on 128 GPUs

other.bitext_upsampling: tuned rate; no upsampling for sampling/beam+noise at 24M; rate 16 for the 226M En-De run; none for En-Fr

inference.decoding: final evaluation: beam 5, no length penalty. Synthetic data generation: greedy, beam 5, unrestricted sampling, top10 sampling (restricted to k=10 most likely tokens, renormalized), beam+noise
inference.samples: one synthetic source sample per target sentence

parameters.noise_blank: replace words by filler token with probability 0.1
parameters.noise_swap: random permutation restricted to swapping words no further than three positions apart

metrics.name: training perplexity
metrics.definition: cross-entropy on 500K sub-sampled synthetic pairs and equal-size bitext subset, per epoch

metrics.name: source-side LM perplexity
metrics.definition: 5-gram Kneser-Ney LM trained on 4.1M real source sentences scoring synthetic sources of 450K held-out pairs

eval.protocol: single runs reported; no seeds, variance or significance tests stated

evidence.quote: Experiments are run on 16 machines and we perform 30K synchronous updates.

results.claim: Back-translation with sampling on 226M German monolingual sentences gives 35 BLEU on WMT'14 En-De newstest2014, new state of the art using only WMT benchmark data.
results.setup: WMT En-De newstest2014, Big Transformer, 5.2M bitext + 226M synthetic, bitext upsample rate 16, 250K updates
results.table: Table 6, row Our result, column En-De
results.note: text rounds to 35; abstract and intro say outperforms DeepL by 1.7 BLEU

results.claim: Detokenized (sacreBLEU) score for the same En-De system is 33.8.
results.table: Table 6, row detok. sacreBLEU, column En-De

results.claim: En-Fr with 31M sampled back-translations reaches 45.6 tokenized BLEU on newstest2014 vs 42.90 bitext only.
results.setup: WMT'14 En-Fr newstest2014, 35.7M bitext + 31M newscrawl by sampling, 300K updates

results.claim: Sampling or noised beam outperforms pure beam search by 1.7 BLEU on average across newstest2013-2017 En-De.
results.setup: WMT En-De, 5.2M bitext + 24M synthetic, average of newstest2013-2017
results.quote: sampling and noised beam outperforms pure beam by 1.7 BLEU on average on newstest2013-2017 for WMT English-German translation
results.note: Table 1 averages: bitext 31.00, beam 31.78, greedy 31.96, top10 32.94, sampling 33.51, beam+noise 33.43

results.claim: Average BLEU with 24M sampled synthetic pairs vs bitext only.
results.setup: WMT En-De newstest2013-2017 average, 5.2M bitext + 24M synthetic by sampling

results.claim: Synthetic data from BT-bitext (sampled) gets 83% of the gain of real bitext when domains match.
results.metric: share of gain from real bitext
results.setup: 640K bitext base; adding BT of remaining bitext target side; newstest2012 En-De
results.quote: BT-bitext improves by 2.2 BLEU, achieving 83% of the improvement with real bitext

results.claim: On mixed-domain valid set, BT-bitext trails real bitext by 1.3 BLEU, 67% of the gain.
results.quote: BT-bitext matches the domain of valid-mixed and improves by 2.7 BLEU
results.note: text: trails real bitext by only 1.3 BLEU, 67% of gain

results.claim: Sampling and beam+noise beat greedy/beam by 0.8-1.1 BLEU on newstest2012 in the largest setup.
results.setup: WMT En-De newstest2012, up to 24M synthetic
results.quote: outperform the MAP methods (pure beam search and greedy) by 0.8-1.1 BLEU

results.claim: Beam-generated synthetic sources are the most predictable for a 5-gram LM (PPL 72.42) vs human 75.34, sampling 500.17, beam+noise 2823.73.
results.setup: 5-gram Kneser-Ney on 4.1M real sources; 450K held-out pairs; BT model on 640K pairs

results.claim: In the 80K-bitext setup, beam beats sampling; with 640K and 5.2M bitext, sampling is better.
results.setup: reverse De-En quality on newstest2012: 80K, 640K, 5M bitext
results.quote: On newstest2012 we measure 13.5 BLEU for 80K bitext, 24.3 BLEU for 640K and 28.3 BLEU for 5M.

results.claim: Beam+noise and sampling need no bitext upsampling; beam and greedy benefit from higher upsample rates.
Training perplexity on beam data falls below 2 after 5 epochs; beam/greedy data is easier to fit than bitext, sampling data harder.
results.quote: the perplexity on beam data falls below 2 after only 5 epochs

limits: Sampling and noise hurt in the very low-resource setup (80K bitext), where beam is better
Sampled/noised sources are sometimes inadequate (Table 3: sampling adds target words absent from source)
Mostly single-direction (En-De) with newswire monolingual data; En-Fr as confirmation only
No seeds, variance or significance tests reported
Authors' future work: optimize the back-translation model end-to-end to produce the most helpful sources
The explanation (richer training signal) is a conjecture supported by training loss and LM perplexity, not a causal test
Comparison with DeepL is not like for like (DeepL uses proprietary high-quality bitext)

terms.definition: first trains an intermediate system on the parallel data which is used to translate the target monolingual data into the source language; the synthetic pairs are added to real bitext to train the final system
beam search outputs transformed by deleting words (p=0.1), replacing words by a filler token (p=0.1) and swapping words within three positions
sampling restricted at each time step to the k most likely tokens (k=10), renormalized
